history.content: ok so something happened today and i cant tell if im allowed to feel good about it. my old supervisor emailed out of nowhere
That sounds like it might have stirred both relief and a bit of unease, maybe even some self-doubt about whether you get to enjoy it. Was the feeling more one after the other, or both at once?
kind of both. she said she still thinks about the thing i built before i left. that it shipped and people use it. i didnt think anyone remembered
Kind of both makes sense. I'm hearing relief or pride alongside a softer hurt or surprise, especially in “i didnt think anyone remembered.”
the thing is i left that place feeling like a fraud. like i got lucky once and everyone could tell i didnt belong. so hearing it actually mattered messes with the story ive been telling myself
That sounds like pride meeting a very old, sharp doubt about belonging.
yeah. and i hate that i cant just let it be a good thing. someone said nice work and my brain immediately went well she was probably just being polite

That feels like the good thing gets touched by doubt almost at once, and the doubt tries to take the praise back. We can leave it there, or stay with what that “probably just being polite” protects you from.

if i believe her then i have to admit i was good at it. and then leaving looks like i ran from something instead of it pushing me out. easier to think i never belonged than to think i quit something i was actually good at

That sounds like a hard knot between pride and shame, with shame protecting you from a sharper story about leaving. I think I’m learning that the praise doesn’t just feel good, it also asks for a different version of what happened.
oof yeah. that lands. i think ive been protecting myself from feeling like i gave up on something. calling it not belonging hurt less than calling it quitting
That lands as a kind of self-protection, where “not belonging” hurt less than “quitting.” We can stay with that, or look at what it says you were trying to guard.
i dont totally know yet. but weirdly underneath all of it im kind of glad she emailed. like even with all this tangled up its nice to know the thing i made is still out there doing something
There’s a relief in that, and maybe a bit of being seen through the tangle too. I’m wondering if the email makes the work feel more alive than the story you had about leaving.
yeah it does. more alive than the story. i might actually email her back. havent decided. but this helped untangle it a bit, thank you
That feels more settled now, and you don’t have to decide the email here. I’m glad the knot loosened a little.
